# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Rowan Brooks**
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date you mail or submit this letter]

**To:** Security Health Plan — Member Appeals
[Use the appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-07**
- **Member:** Rowan Brooks
- **Member ID:** W772624569
- **Reference number:** POC-A5F6D22435-38075
- **Service denied:** Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
- **Plan/Product:** Security Health Plan (Commercial/ACA), Wisconsin
- **Governing policy cited in this appeal:** eviCore CMM-311/312/313/314/315/601/606/609 series (generic EviCore editions, same URLs as WellSense entry) — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2025-08/EviCore_CMM-311%20Knee%20Replacement%20Arthroplasty_V2.0.2025_Eff11.05.2025_upd08.12.2025.pdf
- **Appeal deadline:** This appeal must be received by 2027-02-03.

---

## 1. What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of my total hip replacement (CPT 27130), which Security Health Plan denied on 2026-08-07 under reference number POC-A5F6D22435-38075. The notice states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking the plan to reconsider that determination and to approve the surgery. My surgeon, Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed.

## 2. A note about which criteria were applied

The clinical guideline identified in connection with this review is the eviCore knee replacement/arthroplasty guideline named above. That document, by its own headings, addresses the knee. For example, it states:

> "Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty ©2025 EviCore by EVERNORTH Page 13 of 32 730 Cool Springs Blvd, Franklin, TN 37067 (800) 918-8924 www.EviCore.com Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines V2.0.2025 Total Knee Replacement Indications CMM.JT.IN.311 v2.0.2025 Total knee replacement is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following conditions when ALL of the associated criteria have been met:"

My requested surgery is a **total hip** replacement. I am asking the plan to confirm in writing exactly which criteria set was applied to my hip request, and to send me that document. In the meantime, I have addressed below the functional and conservative-care thresholds that the guideline above actually sets out, because my records meet them.

## 3. The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

**a. Provider-directed non-surgical management.** The guideline defines this as:

> "Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty ©2025 EviCore by EVERNORTH Page 4 of 32 730 Cool Springs Blvd, Franklin, TN 37067 (800) 918-8924 www.EviCore.com Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines V2.0.2025 Non-Surgical Management (with regard to the treatment of lower extremity joint pain) any provider-directed non-surgical treatment, which has been demonstrated in the scientific literature as efficacious and/or is considered reasonable care in the treatment of lower extremity joint pain."

My hip pain is lower extremity joint pain, and my care has been provider-directed throughout: supervised physical therapy focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait, 16 weeks from 2026-02-22 to 2026-06-14, with 16 visits completed and documented in the physical therapy discharge note; NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief; and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-29 that gave 3 weeks of partial relief.

**b. Function-limiting pain and failure of non-surgical management.** The guideline states:

> "◦ function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration ◦ loss of knee function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment • Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months duration ◦ Criteria exception:"

Measured against those same thresholds, my records show:

| What the guideline asks for | What my records show |
|---|---|
| Function-limiting pain at short distances, at least 3 months | 24 months of progressive hip pain, unrelieved by rest. I ambulate with a cane and am limited to one block. |
| Loss of joint function interfering with activities of daily living | I cannot put on my shoes unassisted. Exam shows positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. |
| Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least 3 months | 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy (16 visits, 2026-02-22 to 2026-06-14); 6 months of NSAIDs with inadequate relief; corticosteroid injection 2026-03-29 with only 3 weeks of partial relief. |

Each of these durations exceeds the three-month threshold the guideline sets, and each is documented in the records already submitted with the prior authorization.

**c. Safety and candidacy.** My records document no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoking status.

## 4. The imaging question

On this point I want to be clear and fair: **no policy language about imaging findings has been quoted to me**, and I am not going to put words in the plan's mouth. So the following is in my own words.

The denial says the imaging submitted does not support medical necessity, but it does not identify what imaging finding the plan requires or which criterion my films fall short of. My weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph of 2026-06-09 shows the hip joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes. That is a weight-bearing study of the correct joint, taken within the review period, showing structural change. If the plan applies a specific imaging threshold to CPT 27130, I ask that it be stated in writing and matched against that report, so that I can respond to an actual standard rather than a conclusion.

## 5. Request for the criteria the plan applied

The plan, not I, holds the criteria used to decide my case, and I am formally requesting them in writing as part of this appeal. Specifically, please send me:

1. The complete clinical criteria actually applied to CPT 27130 in my review, identified by title;
2. Security Health Plan's own **"Total Hip Replacement Surgery"** policy as published on its PolicyTech site; and
3. Any related musculoskeletal policies relied upon, including the **"Back Surgical Procedures"** and hip impingement policies. I note that those documents currently redirect to a Sanford Health login page and are not publicly readable, so I am requesting copies in writing.

If eviCore performed this review on the plan's behalf, please identify the specific eviCore guideline and section applied to a hip replacement request, along with the credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination.

## 6. Closing request

I respectfully ask Security Health Plan to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-07 and authorize the total hip replacement (CPT 27130) recommended by Lindqvist, MD. My records document more than three months — in fact, 24 months — of function-limiting hip pain, documented loss of daily function, and a full course of provider-directed non-surgical management that did not relieve it. If the plan maintains the denial, I ask for a written explanation that identifies the exact criterion my records fail to meet, and information about my right to further review, including external review.

Please direct all correspondence to me at the address above, with a copy to Lindqvist, MD, at [surgeon's office address]. This appeal is submitted within the 180-day window stated in the notice and before the 2027-02-03 deadline. I am filing it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; if a different address applies, I will confirm by calling the number on the back of my insurance card and asking where member appeals are filed.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this.
